content.content:
### Editing a picture

`POST /v1/images/edits` answers when the server is started with **`-edits N`**,
where N is how many reference images an edit may carry. The mechanism changed
with the model, and so did what a client sends. Under Z-Image-Turbo this
endpoint did SDEdit: the picture was encoded to a latent, the latent mixed
with noise at an intermediate point on the schedule, and only the tail run —
`strength` being how far back up the schedule that point was.

**Qwen-Image-2.1 does not edit that way.** An edit is a *conditional
generation*: every reference image is resized to the condition area and
encoded twice — by a 27-layer vision tower into context the prompt's tokens
absorb, and by the VAE into latents that become rows of the transformer's own
sequence — and the target is then denoised from pure noise through the whole
schedule, attending over that prefix at every step. Four consequences a
client sees:

- **`strength` is gone.** Nothing is partially renoised, so there is no knob
  to have. A request that still sends one is a 400 saying so, rather than
  having it quietly ignored.
- **An edit costs slightly *more* than a generation**, not less: the prefix
  is thousands of tokens rather than tens. Measured at 1024² with one
  reference, an edit is **1m54s** against a generation's 1m28.8s — the
  reference's own encoding is 7.1 s of it (a 27-layer vision tower and a VAE
  encode), and the rest is the prefix riding along in every denoising step.
- **`image[]` is a real list.** Up to `max_reference_images` pictures are
  accepted, in the order they were sent, and the model's own limit is ten.
  How many *this* server takes is residency — every reference adds its latent
  rows to the prefix and its share of the prefix KV cache — so it is fixed by
  `-edits N` at startup and reported in `GET /v1/models`.
  between texts:
  - chat `image_url`;
  - Responses `input_image` (`image_url` string; `file_id` refused, no files);
  - Messages `image` (base64 source becomes a data URL; a url source passes
    through and is refused).
  **Q3 decided (default): remote URLs are refused** with the fix in the message
  (send the bytes). Audio, video, files and documents stay refused with
  specific reasons. So do images in a tool result or a system prompt (the
  template refuses the latter), and WebP (Q6). `MessageContent.Unreadable`
  replaced `NonText`. **Gates:** `TestImagesReachTheBackend` (all three doors
  deliver text / image / text in order, as a data URL) and the updated refusal
(11.2–11.6 dB against the other one). The model gets there by a cut to the
close-up about two thirds in, not a push-in, which is a fair reading of two
keyframes and a prompt that says nothing about the camera moving.

**Served** (`serve -video`, the README fl2va request with its keyframe
inlined as a data: URI, `short_edge 256`, 5 s, N = 8): the canvas resolves
to 448×256 from the keyframe (`aspect_ratio: "auto"`), estimated 220 s, run
in 3 m 21 s, and the mp4 is **byte-identical** to the CLI's at the same
seed. The README's own request, CDN link and all, is the 400 above.

**Served:** OpenAI's `input_reference` (multipart, or base64/data: URL in
JSON) is the first frame; SGLang's `conditions` are up to two images with
`frame_index` 0 (first) and -1 or ≥ the last requested frame (last).
**A condition's `uri` must be a `data:` URL**: the server does not fetch on
a client's behalf (LLM-VISION.md's rule), so the README scripts' CDN links
are a 400 that says to inline the picture. `task: fl2va` with no keyframe is
t2va, as the model card has it; `t2va` with one and `ref2va` are 400s.

---
name: api-follows-openai-standard
description: The HTTP API does what OpenAI's API does, behaviour included — e.g. image URLs are fetched wherever OpenAI fetches them; don't invent stricter or looser house rules.
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

The API should follow OpenAI's standard, behaviour and not just shape: "if they don't fetch images we don't fetch images. If they do, we do." (user, 2026-09-26). Applied then: `util.FetchImage` fetches http(s)/data: image URLs for chat `image_url`, Responses `input_image`, images/edits `images[].image_url`, videos `input_reference.image_url` and SGLang `conditions[].uri`; `file_id` refused (no Files API). This replaced LLM-VISION.md Q3's "refuse remote URLs" decision.

**Why:** clients written against OpenAI must work unchanged; a house rule that differs silently breaks them.

**How to apply:** when a design question is "what should the endpoint do with X", check OpenAI's API reference first (developers.openai.com/api/reference/...; platform.openai.com 403s to WebFetch) and match it; only deviate where the model can't (and say so in the error). content.text:
The server now downloads images from URLs wherever OpenAI's API does, which turned out to be every place it accepts an image. The video and image-edit reference docs both say an `image_url` can be "a fully qualified URL or base64-encoded data URL" ([videos](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/videos/methods/create), [images](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/cli/resources/images)), and OpenAI's chat `image_url` is fetched too. So the old "`data:` URLs only" rule is gone from all of them. Tests pass, and the README's own `fl2va` request now works against a live server with its CDN link unchanged. I cancelled that job after it queued.

**One download routine for everything** (`util/fetch.go`):
- It takes `http(s)` URLs and `data:` URLs; any other scheme is refused.
- It stops at 50 MB (OpenAI's per-image limit) or 60 s, follows up to 5 redirects, and needs a success status.
- Any failure is a 400 that names the URL, with the query string left out so signed URLs don't leak.

**What changed at each endpoint:**
- **Videos:** `input_reference` now takes OpenAI's JSON object, `{"image_url": …}`, and the URL is downloaded. A bare URL or base64 string is also accepted, and multipart uploads work as before. SGLang's `conditions[].uri` is downloaded the same way. This all happens when the job is submitted, so a picture that can't be read is a 400 rather than a failed job.
- **Chat, Responses, Messages (the LLM's images):** http(s) URLs are downloaded before the vision tower claims the GPU, so a slow download never holds it.
- **Image edits:** they now accept OpenAI's JSON `images: [{"image_url": …}]`, alongside the existing `image` field. A `mask` sent in OpenAI's object form now gets the intended "mask not implemented" 501; before, it was rejected as malformed JSON.
- **`file_id`:** refused everywhere with a clear 400, because there's no Files API here.

**Decision for you:** the server downloads whatever URL the client gives it, including addresses on your local network. That is what OpenAI-compatible servers do, and I haven't added a switch to limit it. Only you can say whether that's acceptable on your network. If it isn't, the fix is an allow/deny list in the download routine or a boundary in front of the server; say if you want the former.

**Docs:** API.md, VIDEO.md, and LLM-VISION.md's Q3 (the old "refuse remote URLs" decision is marked superseded). I also saved "the API follows OpenAI's behaviour, not just its request shapes" as a standing preference in memory.

Nothing is committed; the auto-committer will pick it up.
